F. CLIMATE AND AIR QUALITY
Section II—F dealing with the description of Climate and Air Quality established that motor vehicle traffic is the major contributor to air pollution. It has also been established that, with the exception of Alviso, the target neighborhoods in the Community Development Block Grant program are all currently affected by heavy automotive traffic and its resulting pollutant emissions. The rehabilitation, capital improvement and public facility projects proposed for the three-year CDBG program will not significantly affect the volumes of traffic on the various neighborhood streets. Section III—F, addressing Traffic and Circulation has shown that traffic volumes will increase in the future on many of the major streets affecting the CNRA's, irregardless of the Block Grant program. Any air quality impacts of the neighborhoods resulting from the continuation or initiation of Block Grant programs, then will derive from another sources.
The program's principal air quality impact will be the increase in the local concentration of total suspended particulates (TSP) raised during housing rehabilitations, demolitions, excavation and trenching for sewer lines, and grading and paving for street improvements and park improvements.
